archetypes.name: state-machine-coherence
archetypes.rationale: The plan introduces a formal 4-state Resume-phase model with 4 bail-out classes and 5 terminal states; inconsistent phase writes or missing transitions could cause double-apply or stranded rounds in ways the generic correctness slot may not enumerate exhaustively across all cross-referenced FINDINGs.
archetypes.prompt_body: Check the plan's Resume-phase model transitions for completeness and consistency: verify every bail-out writes the correct phase atomically before emitting its envelope; verify every resume entry reads the phase and branches exactly as specified; and identify any state from which no defined exit exists or any path that could write a phase without the corresponding artifact (e.g., the loop pre-apply snapshot or the .gate-b-postapply-ready-N marker). Cross-check the nine FINDING annotations for internal consistency: specifically FINDING_2 (panel-failed persists vs. tally-error rolls back review-round-count.txt), FINDING_3 (main-agent-apply-required bail-out ends with the loop re-entering at awaiting-continuation, never at awaiting-apply), FINDING_5 (postplan-failed is a hard-fail abort, not a Step 3b transition), and FINDING_8 (MAV re-tally yielding 0 accepted promotes directly to awaiting-continuation without triggering apply). Flag any plan section where the described phase transition sequence contradicts another section's description of the same transition. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: prior-art-contract-fit
archetypes.rationale: The plan integrates revise-plan-with-waterfall.sh as prior art that was never wired in; the plan's correctness depends on its argv, KV output fields, and failure semantics exactly matching the actual script contract, which the generic architecture slot may not verify file-by-file.
archetypes.prompt_body: Read skills/design/scripts/revise-plan-with-waterfall.sh and its companion contract document (revise-plan-with-waterfall.md if present) and compare them against what the plan claims about the reviser's interface. Verify that every KV field the plan reads from the reviser (REVISE_STATUS, REVISE_TIER_1..4_STATUS, REVISE_WINNING_TIER, REVISE_PATCH_PATH, REVISE_PLAN_HASH_BEFORE, REVISE_PLAN_HASH_AFTER) actually appears in the contract, and that --patch-format file-replacement is a valid argv option. Check whether the plan correctly handles the reviser's own plan.txt.before-revise deletion-on-success: the plan states the loop pre-apply snapshot is the dedup-failure restore source precisely because the reviser deletes its own snapshot on success — verify this behavioral guarantee is present in the reviser contract and consistently reflected in the plan's edge-cases section. Confirm the --findings-file and --round-num argv conventions match the actual reviser signature, and flag any field, option, or behavioral guarantee cited in the plan that the actual script does not expose. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
